name: Lasers
kicker: Focused beam of coherent light · From barcode scanners to eye surgery
briefing: A laser produces an intensely focused beam of coherent light, meaning every light wave lines up in step at exactly one wavelength, unlike the scattered light from a regular bulb. Theodore Maiman built the first one in 1960 using a ruby crystal, and at first the new invention was jokingly called “a solution looking for a problem.” Today lasers cut steel, play DVDs, scan barcodes, and correct eyesight in surgery.
answerHtml: Lasers (or light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation)
accept: light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation

trap.title: Laser, or maser?
trap.body: A maser works the same way but amplifies microwaves instead of visible light, and it was actually built a few years before this device. Real answer lines prompt on “maser” rather than rejecting it outright, since both devices rely on the same stimulated-emission process.
trap.fix: If the clues mention visible or infrared light, ruby or dye gain media, or barcode scanners and DVDs, it is safely this device. If the clues instead say “microwave,” it may want “maser.”
trap.line: Real answer line: Lasers [or light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation; prompt on “masers”]
